{{Quote|Now then, Sarsius, my drumheller harp, please. For I have a promise to keep... to a Dark Lord.|Zeta Mangus requesting Sarsius Torne to bring him his drumheller harp|<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />}}
The '''drumheller harp''' was a [[Music/Legends|percussion]] instrument that had attachments such as the [[O'Tawa cymbal/Legends|O'Tawa cymbal]], a [[screamer gong]], and a [[Tryna chime]]. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]] directed a [[Sarsius Torne|servant]] to bring him his harp while at [[Rennek palace]] in the [[Dark Worlds]]. In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the instrument was used by the [[Drum/Legends|drummer]] [[Ak-rev/Legends|Ak-rev]] while he and the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] performed the song "[[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]]" in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==Description==
The drumheller harp was a [[Color/Legends|brown]]-colored [[Music/Legends|percussion]] instrument that could have a variety of attachments.<ref name="CSWE" /> The instrument was constructed with a circular harp base at the bottom, above which one resonator and two [[O'Tawa cymbal/Legends|O'Tawa cymbals]],<ref name="TVD" /> that formed the heart of the instrument,<ref name="CSWECymbal">{{CSWECite|II|429|O'Tawa cymbals}}</ref> were located. Six<ref name="TVD" /> [[centressar strings]]<ref name="CSWE" /> were attached between the base and the resonator. A circular chime mount that contained a<ref name="TVD" /> [[Tryna chime]]<ref name="CSWE" /> was also connected to the resonator.<ref name="TVD" /> A [[screamer gong]]<ref name="CSWE" /> was held atop a gong stand connected to the harp base. [[Seilith music charms]] were wrapped around the stand.<ref name="TVD" />

The instrument could be played by either plucking its strings<ref name="SkyeWalkers" /> or by hitting either its O'Tawa cymbals or the screamer gong with<ref name="VI" /> a gong mallet.<ref name="SWTSE">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> The drumheller harp was considered to be marvelous and its sound to be mellifluous.<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />

==History==
{{Quote|I have taken the time to memorize the languages of each and all my victims&mdash;the process demands but a few hours, akin to my learning the Mawanese vioflute, the drumheller harp, or Zeltronian lute.|Zeta Magnus reflects on his abilities|<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />}}
[[File:DrumhellerHarp-ROTJ.png|thumb|400px|right|Ak-rev played the drumheller harp at Jabba's palace.]]
By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="SeWsDate">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]'' dates itself to be between the events of {{Film|II}} and ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' and {{FactFile2014|24|22 BBY 85-86|The Struggle for Toydaria}} respectively date Episode II and the [[Ambush|first episode]] of ''The Clone Wars'' to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. Therefore, ''SkyeWalkers'' must take place within that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> the [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanian]] [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic]] [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]] had learned how to play the drumheller harp within a few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]]. By that [[Local year|year]] as well, one of the instruments was owned by Magnus and placed in [[Rennek palace]] in the [[Dark Worlds]]. While at the palace, the Arkanian directed [[Sarsius Torne]], a [[Thyrsian]] [[Sun Guard]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] who served him, to bring him his instrument, to which he played as he released a plague onto the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="SkyeWalkers" />

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|VI}} to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]</ref> a drumheller harp was present in the throne room of [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]<ref name="VI" /> [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="Complete Locations">''[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|Star Wars: Complete Locations]]''</ref> The instrument was used alongside<ref name="VI" /> the [[power drum]]<ref name="Complete Locations" /> by the [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] [[Drum/Legends|drummer]] [[Ak-rev/Legends|Ak-rev]] when he<ref name="SWTSE" /> performed the song "[[Jedi Rocks/Legends|Jedi Rocks]]" with the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] shortly before the arrival of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] member [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], disguised as [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boushh/Legends|Boushh]]. The drumheller harp was removed from the throne room<ref name="VI" /> when [[Local day/Legends|night]] fell that day.<ref name="JN">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The drumheller harp first appeared in the ''[[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]]'' re-release of the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="VI" /> The re-release premiered on [[March 14]], [[1997]],<ref name="A Gift For Boba Fett">{{ThisWeek|KUPQ8aT8bJU|Marvel Comics Previews, Unwrapping a Gift for Boba Fett, and More!}}</ref> ahead of the harp's reveal<ref name="Galaxy10">{{GalaxyCite|10|Renewing the Universe}}</ref> in [[January]] [[1997]]<ref name="Galaxy10Date">{{GalaxyCite|9|Around the Galaxy}}</ref> in the "[[Squib/Legends|Renewing the Universe]]" article of the [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine|tenth]] issue of ''[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine]]''.<ref name="Galaxy10" /> The instrument was first identified in ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'', a [[1998]] reference book written by [[David West Reynolds (real person)|David West Reynolds]].<ref name="TVD" /> The capitalization of the instrument was later provided in the [[2008]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Stephen J. Sansweet]].<ref name="CSWE" />
